text.p: Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera on Thursday ridiculed economic forecasters as failed "astrologers" who use mathematical incantations to prophesize economic disaster.
"There are some people who don't give things their due ... and we could call them economic astrologers," Caldera said.
"They make calculations, invoke the planets and say inflation will be huge, the devaluation spontaneous... But my reply to their prophecies is, fortunately, they will not come true."

Caldera spoke during a televised broadcast after he ceremonially signed into law a $14 billion ground-breaking Labour Law reform that paves the way for a revamping of the country's decaying social security system.

Private forecasters say the free-spending bill will jeopardise tough International Monetary Fund economic reforms launched last year and boost inflation beyond the 35 percent official year-end target.

"Astrology is not at its most prestigious level in this country after the recently failed prediction that I would physically or politically die," added Caldera, referring to local astrologer Jose Bernardo Gomez.

Gomez became a cause celebre after he was briefly detained by police in October for predicting the President would be ousted from office on June 8. At 81, Caldera is Latin America's oldest leader and has been dogged in recent months by rumours of ill health.
Gomez admitted last week he probably made a mistake.
